Aminos in Canada — What Every Listing Shows

Not everything on a peptide shelf is a peptide, and this category keeps the ones that are not from being shelved as if they were. NAD+ is a dinucleotide coenzyme, studied in cellular-energetics and ageing models for its role in redox reactions and as a substrate for the sirtuins and PARPs. Glutathione is a tripeptide (γ-glutamyl-cysteinyl-glycine) — technically a peptide, but studied as the cell’s principal small-molecule antioxidant rather than as a signalling peptide, which is why it sits here with the cofactors rather than with BPC-157.

The quantities are larger than on the peptide shelf — 500 mg and 1000 mg vials of NAD+, 1500 mg of glutathione — and that changes what to read on the certificate. Purity is the usual figure; measured content is the one that matters at this scale, because a 1500 mg label that holds 1350 mg is a different product. Both are published for every lot, against the batch code on the vial.

Both compounds are sensitive to light and moisture in solution, and the product pages state the storage condition. Supplied strictly for laboratory research use, shipped within Canada.

records.title: NAD+
records.description:
NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) is a coenzyme found in all living cells and plays a central role in cellular redox reactions. It is supplied for controlled laboratory research involving metabolic and mitochondrial signaling systems.
In scientific literature, NAD+ is studied in experimental models examining oxidative phosphorylation, sirtuin-associated pathways, and cellular energy regulation mechanisms under in vitro and preclinical research conditions.
Overview
NAD+ is a fundamental coenzyme involved in redox reactions, cellular respiration, and energy metabolism research. Experimental studies examine its role in mitochondrial function models, sirtuin-related signaling pathways, and oxidative stress response systems within controlled laboratory environments.
Preclinical and biochemical research publications have explored its involvement in metabolic regulatory frameworks and enzymatic signaling cascades.
History
NAD+ was first identified in the early 20th century during investigations into fermentation and cellular respiration. Over time, it became recognized as a critical cofactor in metabolic reactions and enzymatic processes.
Subsequent research expanded into studies of its role in mitochondrial function, energy metabolism, and cellular regulatory systems within experimental models.
Research
Laboratory investigations into NAD+ have focused on cellular energy metabolism models, mitochondrial signaling pathways, and redox-regulated enzymatic systems. Research frameworks evaluate its role in sirtuin activation models, oxidative phosphorylation systems, and metabolic regulatory mechanisms under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.

records.title: Glutathione
records.description:
Glutathione is an endogenous tripeptide (γ-Glu-Cys-Gly) studied in research as a principal cellular antioxidant and redox regulator.
Experimental models examine its role in oxidative-stress defense and detoxification pathways under controlled laboratory conditions.
Overview
Glutathione is the most abundant intracellular thiol antioxidant, central to redox homeostasis, detoxification, and protection against oxidative stress. Research has examined its antioxidant activity, depletion under stress, and effects of supplementation in model systems.
Studies span hepatic, high-altitude/hypoxic, and inflammatory research frameworks under structured conditions.
History
Glutathione has been studied for over a century as a core component of cellular antioxidant defense.
Contemporary research continues to examine its metabolism, depletion, and supplementation across diverse stress models.
Research
Research into glutathione focuses on redox homeostasis and oxidative-stress defense. Frameworks evaluate antioxidant capacity, detoxification, and supplementation endpoints under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.

Cellular redox-homeostasis models
Oxidative-stress defense research
Detoxification-pathway studies
Antioxidant supplementation frameworks
